text:
Situation: FDA's shortage list shows Amino Acid Injection from Baxter Healthcare as a current shortage first posted on 2020-12-08. As of 2026-10-21 the shortage has been on FDA's list for 70 months. Corvale East holds 21 bags providing 4.8 days on hand at current use. Corvale General holds 63 bags providing 14 days on hand at current use.

Why (FDA record): FDA has not posted a manufacturing or quality reason for the shortage.

Our position: Inventory at Corvale East is critical. Corvale General supply is limited. No alternative Baxter supply is available. Conservation and allocation are required immediately.

Recommended actions:
1. Restrict Corvale East stock to neonatal and pediatric patients only; Pharmacy Director approves.
2. Limit Corvale General distribution to ICU and TPN-dependent inpatients; Pharmacy Director approves.
3. Activate emergency purchase of alternative amino acid injection from non-Baxter suppliers; P&T Committee Chair and CFO approve.
4. Implement daily inventory tracking and twice-weekly status reports to P&T Committee; Pharmacy Buyer executes.
5. Develop criteria for compounding or alternative PN formulations if commercial supply exhausts; Clinical Nutrition Manager and P&T Committee approve.

Not recommended: Initiating compounding without sterility validation; switching patients to oral amino acids without clinician order; delaying emergency purchase pending Baxter restock.
